rationale: The spec is unusually well-fenced (R3.4's hint-class fence and R3.5's one-phase.Cache/no-new-API bar are concrete and falsifiable; OQ-1's three options genuinely coexist with R4's ACs; AC-1/3/5/9/10/11/12 are runnable and red-on-revert as written). But the pairwise scan finds four MAJOR consistency/coverage defects. (1) R1.3's agreement-table contract quietly forecloses OQ-3 option 2 while OQ-3 claims to be open: I verified derive.go returns the STORED phase after emitting the mismatch warning ('trusting stored phase'), so post-plan-approve `state show` reports `implement` while DerivePhaseFromChildren says `plan` — the row's required three-surface agreement on `plan` is unsatisfiable under option 2 ('table documents stored-leads-derived as designed'), and AC-2 masks this by testing only the derivation surface, the one surface that agrees with the row. (2) Background asserts #220 'reproduces at HEAD, both shapes', but the main-checkout shape ({"mode":"idle"} with no activeSpec field while a draft is active) is pinned by no requirement and no AC — R1.1's rule requires idle-AND-non-empty-activeSpec, and AC-1 is scoped to the draft worktree — so an implementation passes every AC with that shape intact. (3) R6.2's 'R6.3 makes any drop loud rather than silent' overstates R6.3, whose text and AC-10 cover only the positional-error path; I verified both list paths (next.go step 2.5 and runEmitOnly) drop filtered beads silently, so the pick-N-vs-bd-row index shift the Background itself documents as residue #2 is neither fixed, made loud, nor cleanly deferred (#255's deferral covers only the empty-set 'no ready work' outcome). (4) R2.1 pins result-before-tail ordering for seven verbs; AC-3/AC-4 test two of them. These are spec-document fixes, not design reversals — hence REQUEST_CHANGES, no hard block.
concrete_changes_required: R1.3 + AC-2: state which surfaces each agreement-table fixture asserts. Either (a) make AC-2 assert `state show`/tail output per row (not only DerivePhaseFromChildren, which is the one surface that already agrees with the plan-approve row), and carve the plan-approve row so that under OQ-3 option 2 it may be an annotated stored-vs-derived row rather than a three-surface agreement; or (b) strike OQ-3 option 2 and stop claiming the OQ is open on that axis. As written, the row's 'agree on plan' contract is unsatisfiable under option 2 (derive.go trusts stored `implement`) while OQ-3 claims all options live.

Give the #220 main-checkout shape an explicit disposition: add an AC (or extend AC-1) covering `mindspec state show` from a non-worktree checkout while a draft spec exists, or record it as an explicit OQ-2-conditional deferral in Non-Goals. Today the Background presents it as reproducing evidence but no requirement or AC pins it — R1.1 only forbids idle-with-non-empty-activeSpec, and the main-checkout output has no activeSpec field.

Fix the R6.2/R6.3 seam: either add a requirement + AC that the step-2.5 spec-filter announces dropped beads on the list/display paths (e.g. 'N ready beads excluded by spec filter'), or strike R6.2's 'R6.3 makes any drop loud rather than silent' and explicitly record the --pick-N-vs-bd-ready-row-N index shift as deferred alongside #255. R6.3's text and AC-10 cover only the positional-ID error path.

Extend the R2.1 ordering pin beyond two verbs: add a (table-driven) AC asserting result-lines-before-instruct-tail for all seven listed verbs (spec create, spec approve, plan approve, next, complete, impl approve, impl adopt), or scope R2.1 down to the verbs the ACs actually pin.

AC-7: add the mixed-delta case (one post-review delta touching both `.beads/**` and a non-tracker path must still trip the stale-SHA gate) — 'a non-tracker commit' is ambiguous about mixed commits, and mixed is the likeliest silent-widening vector. Also either define how 'tool-authored' in R4.2's pin is verified (the only named mechanism is diff pathspec, which cannot see authorship) or drop 'tool-authored' from the pin so the implemented exemption's true shape (paths-only) is what the spec claims.

R5.1 / AC-8: name at least one concrete claim-written path in the invoking checkout, or state the disposition if the enumeration turns out empty (guard never fires; AC-8's refusal branch is vacuous). The spec currently gestures at 'mindspec state/session files' without establishing the set is non-empty.

OQ-5: correct the closing claim — AC-9 exercises only explicit --pick and pins bd-ready order for the set; it does not pin the default-selection choice. Add an assertion (in AC-9 or a sibling) for the no-pick default path's required self-describing output line ('Defaulting to first item' naming the ordering rule), which R6.2 requires but no AC tests.

findings.title: R1.3's plan-approve row forecloses OQ-3 option 2 while OQ-3 claims to be open; AC-2 tests the one surface that hides it
findings.detail: R1.3 requires each table row pin the mode that `state show`, the instruct tail, and DerivePhaseFromChildren AGREE on, and pins plan-approve → plan. Verified at the reviewed tree: internal/phase/derive.go's stored-phase branch returns storedPhase after the warning ('trusting stored phase'), so with the plan.go:455 `implement` write intact (OQ-3 option 2), `state show` reports `implement` in the post-plan-approve window while DerivePhaseFromChildren returns `plan` (derive.go all-open branch). Three-surface agreement on `plan` is unsatisfiable under option 2 — the option OQ-3 explicitly keeps open ('the table then documents stored-leads-derived in this one window as designed behavior', which is an annotation, not an agreement). AC-2 compounds this: it asserts only 'the shipped derivation produces the row's mode', so the fixture tests DerivePhaseFromChildren (which says plan) and passes while state show and the tail disagree with the table — the AC does not pin the requirement it cites. This is the quiet-OQ-dependency pattern: R1.3 works cleanly only under OQ-3 options 1 or 3.

findings.title: #220's main-checkout shape is evidence but not requirement: every AC passes with `{"mode":"idle"}`-during-active-draft from main intact
findings.detail: Background: '#220 ... reproduces at HEAD, both shapes', and Goal (a) promises verbs 'report the phase the system is actually in'. But the main-checkout capture is `{"mode": "idle"}` with NO activeSpec field, so R1.1's rule (never idle TOGETHER WITH a non-empty activeSpec) does not bite, R1.1's positive rule is preconditioned on 'spec directory + branch exist' (the spec directory is not in a main checkout's working tree), and AC-1 is scoped 'from a fresh no-epic draft spec's worktree'. No other requirement or AC touches the main-checkout case. An implementation satisfying all 13 ACs can leave the main-checkout lie unchanged. If discovery-from-main is intentionally OQ-2-dependent or deferred, the spec must say so explicitly; right now the Goal/Background claim wider honesty than the falsifiability surface delivers.

findings.title: R6.2 cites R6.3 for a guarantee R6.3 does not make: list-path filter drops stay silent, so the documented pick-N index shift is neither fixed nor deferred
findings.detail: R6.2: 'equality with bd ready's own row N holds exactly when the step-2.5 filter drops nothing, and R6.3 makes any drop loud rather than silent.' R6.3's actual requirement (and AC-10) covers only a POSITIONAL bead ID excluded by the filter. Verified at the reviewed tree: both list paths — cmd/mindspec/next.go step 2.5 and runEmitOnly's copy of the same filter — silently rebuild `items` with no output when beads are dropped. So with 3 bd-ready beads and one filtered, `--pick 2` selects bd's row 3 with no signal, the exact 'index shift' Background residue #2 documents. The #255 deferral covers only the empty-after-filter 'no ready work' outcome, not the nonempty-but-shifted case. Either the drop-announcement belongs in R6.3 with an AC, or the index shift must be named as deferred; currently the spec's own cross-reference papers over the gap.

findings.title: R2.1 pins ordering for seven verbs; ACs pin two
findings.detail: R2.1: every state-changing verb (spec create, spec approve, plan approve, next, complete, impl approve, impl adopt) prints result before tail, 'pinned by test rather than incidental'. AC-3 covers spec create; AC-4 covers complete. No AC covers the other five verbs' ordering or tail-mode agreement, so an implementation passes the AC surface while `next` or `impl approve` still emits guidance-before-result (or idle guidance on success — the exact #245 class). Since the ACs are declared 'the falsifiability surface you are judging' (BRIEF) and R2's diagnostic-strings-are-first-class preamble demands red-on-revert tests, the five unpinned verbs are a requirement-without-AC hole.

findings.title: AC-7 is green-at-HEAD and leaves two widening axes untested (mixed deltas; the unverifiable 'tool-authored' qualifier)
findings.detail: AC-7 is not red-on-revert — the stale-SHA gate already blocks everything at HEAD, so the test passes before and after implementation; it is an anti-widening fence, legitimate only in tandem with red-at-HEAD AC-6, and the spec should say so. More substantively: (1) 'a non-tracker commit' is ambiguous about a MIXED delta touching both `.beads/**` and a user path — the likeliest accidental widening (a pathspec check written as 'contains tracker paths' rather than 'confined to tracker paths' passes AC-6 and a plausible reading of AC-7 while exempting mixed deltas). (2) R4.2 pins 'tool-authored, tracker-paths-only, verified by diff pathspec' — but pathspec cannot verify authorship, no AC tests authorship, and no verification mechanism for 'tool-authored' is named; the implemented exemption will be paths-only, so the pin overstates what is enforced.

findings.title: AC-8's refusal branch presupposes a non-empty claim-written path set the spec never establishes
findings.detail: R5.1 defines blocking dirt as 'paths the claim writes in the invoking checkout (mindspec state/session files; .beads/** already artifact-exempt)' but never names one such path. If planning finds the set empty (claim writes only .beads/** plus the new worktree), AC-8's second half ('with dirt on a claim-written path ... it refuses') is untestable and the guard never fires — a de-facto guard removal the spec neither states nor prices. Name one concrete path or state the empty-set disposition.

findings.title: OQ-5 mischaracterizes AC-9, and R6.2's required default-announcement has no AC
findings.detail: OQ-5 closes with 'AC-9's ordering assertion pins whichever choice is made', but AC-9 exercises only explicit `--pick 1/2` and pins the SET's order to bd-ready order; it never exercises the no-pick default path, which is the entire subject of OQ-5. R6.2's requirement that the default selection print a self-describing line naming the ordering rule is likewise untested by any AC. (Read charitably, R6.2 sentence 1 — no post-query reordering — plus OQ-5 coexist only if a plan-order default means 'select lowest-bead-number from the bd-ordered display', not 'reorder the display'; worth one clarifying clause so the plan cannot satisfy OQ-5 by reordering, which would contradict R6.2 and AC-9.)

findings.title: AC-6's diff-pathspec assertion is vacuous under OQ-1 (a) and (b)
findings.detail: Under reorder (a) or rollback (b) the retry sees no delta at all (tip stays at / returns to SHA A), so 'the delta the gate ignored was confined to .beads/**' is trivially true of an empty diff. The assertion is substantive only under exemption (c). This does not break the 'ACs hold under any of (a)/(b)/(c)' claim, but the AC should note the vacuity so a plan choosing (a)/(b) does not cite the assertion's pass as evidence of exemption narrowness — that job then falls entirely to AC-7.

findings.title: AC-4's agreement clause and indeterminate clause need explicit scoping
findings.detail: AC-4 requires the tail 'agrees with Result.NextMode' and, on no-phase resolution, contains the indeterminate marker. As written it is arguable that an implementation rendering the indeterminate marker in ALL cases satisfies both clauses (nothing states the agreement clause applies exactly when context resolution succeeds). One sentence scoping the two clauses to disjoint conditions closes it.
